resolved.title: 模块 Module
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Modules[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

It is a good practice to divide your related code into modules. Before ES6 there were some libraries which made this possible (e.g., RequireJS, CommonJS). ES6 is now supporting this feature natively.

[b]Considerations when using modules:[/b]
The first consideration is [b]maintainability[/b]. A module is independent of other modules, making improvements and expansion possible without any dependency on code in other modules.

The second consideration is [b]namespacing[/b]. In an earlier lesson, we talked about variables and scope. As you know, vars are globally declared, so it's common to have namespace pollution where unrelated variables are accessible all over our code. Modules solve this problem by creating a private space for variables.

Another important consideration is [b]reusability[/b]. When we write code that can be used in other projects, modules make it possible to easily reuse the code without having to rewrite it in a new project.

Let's see how we should use modules in JS files.
[b][/b][s0l0!-header][b]For Example[/b]:[/s0l0!-header] [code format="js" ]// lib/math.js
[b]export[/b] let sum = (x, y) => { return x + y; }
[b]export[/b] let pi = 3.14;

// app.js
[b]import *[/b] as math from "lib/math"
console.log(`2p = + ${math.sum(math.pi, math.pi)}`)[/code]
Here we are exporting the sum function and the pi variable so we can use them in different files.
[note]ES6 supports [b]modules [/b]officially, however, some browsers are not supporting modules natively yet. So, we should use bundlers (builders) such as Webpack or Browserify to run our code.[/note]

It is a good practice to divide your related code into modules. Before ES6 there were some libraries which made this possible (e.g., RequireJS, CommonJS). ES6 is now supporting this feature natively.

**Considerations when using modules:**
The first consideration is **maintainability**. A module is independent of other modules, making improvements and expansion possible without any dependency on code in other modules.

The second consideration is **namespacing**. In an earlier lesson, we talked about variables and scope. As you know, vars are globally declared, so it's common to have namespace pollution where unrelated variables are accessible all over our code. Modules solve this problem by creating a private space for variables.

Another important consideration is **reusability**. When we write code that can be used in other projects, modules make it possible to easily reuse the code without having to rewrite it in a new project.

Let's see how we should use modules in JS files.
**For Example**:

**使用模块时的考虑因素：**。
第一个考虑因素是**可维护性**，一个模块独立于其他模块，使得改进和扩展成为可能。

第二个考虑因素是**命名空间**。在前面的课程中，我们谈到了变量和范围。正如你所知道的，变量是全局声明的，所以通常会出现命名空间污染的情况，即不相关的变量可以在我们的代码中到处被访问。模块通过为变量创建一个私有空间来解决这个问题。

另一个重要的考虑是**可复用性**。当我们希望代码在其他项目中也能使用时，模块使得我们可以轻松地重用这些代码，而不必在新项目中重写一遍。

resolved.title: 内置方法
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Built-in Methods[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

ES6 also introduced new built-in methods to make several tasks easier. Here we will cover the most common ones.

[s0l0!-header][h2]Array Element Finding[/h2][/s0l0!-header] 
The legacy way to find the first element of an array by its value and a rule was the following:[code format="js" codeId="1942"][4, 5, 1, 8, 2, 0].filter(function (x) {
  return x > 3;
})[0];[/code]
The new syntax is cleaner and more robust:[code format="js" codeId="1943"][4, 5, 1, 8, 2, 0].[b]find[/b](x => x > 3);[/code]
You can also get the index of the item above by using the [b]findIndex()[/b] method:[code format="js" codeId="1944"][4, 5, 1, 8, 2, 0].[b]findIndex[/b](x => x > 3);[/code]
[s0l0!-header][h2]Repeating Strings[/h2][/s0l0!-header] 
Before ES6 the following syntax was the correct way to repeat a string multiple times:[code format="js" codeId="1945"]console.log(Array(3 + 1).join("foo")); // foofoofoo[/code]
With the new syntax, it becomes:[code format="js" codeId="1946"]console.log("foo".[b]repeat[/b](3)); // foofoofoo[/code]
[s0l0!-header][h2]Searching Strings[/h2][/s0l0!-header] 
Before ES6 we only used the indexOf() method to find the position of the text in the string. For example:[code format="js" codeId="1947"]"SoloLearn".indexOf("Solo") === 0; // true
"SoloLearn".indexOf("Solo") === (4 - "Solo".length); // true
"SoloLearn".indexOf("loLe") !== -1; // true
"SoloLearn".indexOf("olo", 1) !== -1; // true
"SoloLearn".indexOf("olo", 2) !== -1; // false[/code]
ES6 has replaced this with a version that has cleaner and more simplified syntax:[code format="js" codeId="1948"]"SoloLearn".[b]startsWit[/b]h("Solo", 0); // true
"SoloLearn".[b]endsWith[/b]("Solo", 4); // true
"SoloLearn".[b]includes[/b]("loLe"); // true
"SoloLearn".[b]includes[/b]("olo", 1); // true
"SoloLearn".[b]includes[/b]("olo", 2); // false[/code]
[note]It is always a good practice to refactor your code with the new syntax to learn new things and make your code more understandable.[/note]
